children: Wall Street's major averages were mixed on Friday, while technology stocks continued to lag amid artificial intelligence spending fears and a continued rise in oil prices due to geopolitical turmoil.
The benchmark S&P 500 (
) was last -0.2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite
was +0.2%, and the blue-chip Dow
was -1%.
Big tech stocks, including Amazon
-0.5%, Alphabet
-0.1%, and Meta
-0.3%, continued to suffer.

“Meta’s enormous capex plans have investors questioning whether all that spending will eventually produce an adequate return, while some of the more leveraged infrastructure names are facing a considerably less hospitable financing environment,” said Guy LeBas, Janney's chief fixed income strategist.

“I’m not convinced this means the investment cycle is about to collapse and it’s normal to have repeated retrenchments in a run like we’ve had, but financing costs have a way of turning theoretical spending plans into somewhat smaller actual spending plans,” he added. “Given the size of the AI buildout, that would matter for growth, corporate bond supply, and ultimately rates.”
U.S. President Donald Trump accused Iran of “doing everything they can to drive up the price of oil” prior to the midterm election.
Oil prices rose after reports that the U.S. and Israel could be drawing plans for attacks on Iran.
Crude oil futures (
) rose to $102.13, while Brent (
) was also higher at $116.12 per barrel.

to 57.6, as expected, according to S&P Global on Friday. In addition, the U.S. Manufacturing PMI rose higher than consensus, while the U.S. Services PMI was slightly lower than expected.
